questions.q: What parameters shape which transactions appear on a given customer statement run?
options: Only the customer's credit limit
A statement cycle and date range (cutoff), which determine which customers and transactions are included
Only the supplier's payment terms
The GL chart of accounts structure
questions.explain: A statement run is shaped by cycle and date-range parameters that define exactly which transactions, as of a cutoff, are included.

questions.q: Why was invoice INV-11284 missing from Ridge & Pine Outfitters' statement?
options: The invoice had a hold on it
The invoice was never entered in Receivables
AutoInvoice rejected the transaction
The invoice was dated one day after the statement cycle's cutoff date, correctly excluding it from that run
questions.explain: The invoice, dated the 29th, fell one day outside the statement cycle's cutoff of the 28th, so it was legitimately excluded from that particular run.

questions.q: What did the investigation confirm about the invoice itself?
options: It was correctly accounted, open, and carried no holds
It was misapplied to the wrong customer
It had been accidentally deleted
It had an invalid tax rate code
questions.explain: The investigation confirmed the invoice was legitimate and correctly recorded — the issue was purely a timing boundary on the statement run, not a data problem.

questions.q: What was the correct resolution for this ticket?
options: Modify the invoice date so it would appear on the statement
Reverse and re-enter the invoice
Explain the timing boundary to the customer, confirm the invoice is valid, and send a copy directly if needed sooner
Escalate to Oracle support as a system defect
questions.explain: Since nothing was actually wrong with the data, the resolution was explanation and customer communication rather than any data correction.

questions.q: Why does the resolution note recommend flagging the cutoff timing to AR management rather than just closing the ticket?
options: Because the cutoff date must always be changed immediately
Because if invoices dated near month-end routinely cause this confusion, it's worth considering as a process question rather than repeatedly explaining it ticket by ticket
Because Oracle requires a formal change request for every statement question
Because the customer demanded a policy change
questions.explain: A recurring pattern of confusion around the cutoff date is worth raising as a broader process question to AR management, rather than silently handling it the same way on every future ticket.
